manifest.name: dsh-web-search-free
manifest.description: Free keyless web search (Mojeek/Bing/DuckDuckGo HTML scraping) and local HTTP fetch providers for the DeepSeek Harness web seam (ctx.web) — no API key, no cloud relay

bundle.text:
# dsh-web-search-free bundle layer: free, keyless web access for the seam.
#
# Inserts the provider plugin and points ctx.web at it. This layer applies
# after dsh-base/dsh-web-app (whose base row selects `deepseek-official`),
# and the profile's own cordis.patch.yml still applies after this one, so a
# deployment can always switch `searchProvider` back to another registered
# provider without removing this plugin.

- insert:
    - id: web-search-free
      name: dsh-web-search-free
      config:
        # Engine fallback order; first engine that returns results wins.
        # Available: ddg-lite, ddg-html, mojeek, bing
        engines: [ddg-lite, ddg-html, mojeek, bing]
        # Per-engine HTTP budget in milliseconds.
        timeoutMs: 15000
        # Provider-level source cap (the tool's searchMaxResults still applies).
        maxResults: 10
        # Optional: fetch.maxBodyBytes, fetch.userAgent

# Point the web seam at the free local providers. Registration alone is not
# enough: the base row pre-selects `deepseek-official`, so this override is
# what actually routes web_search (and web_fetch once a composition enables
# it) through the keyless providers.
- id: web
  config:
    searchProvider: free-local
    fetchProvider: free-local-fetch

readme.text: **Free, keyless web access** for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH). This is a DSH *bundle* that registers two local providers into the web seam (`ctx.web`):

| Provider | Id | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `FreeSearchProvider` | `free-local` | powers the `web_search` tool by querying public search engines directly (no DeepSeek cloud, no API key) |
| `LocalFetchProvider` | `free-local-fetch` | powers the `web_fetch` tool by retrieving any HTTP(S) URL directly from your machine |
It replaces `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-search-deepseek`, which requires a paid `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`. Requests go **directly from your machine** to the search engine sites: no intermediary.
The provider tries the engines in order, one at a time, and uses the first one that returns results:

| Engine | Endpoint | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ddg-lite` | `lite.duckduckgo.com` | minimal HTML endpoint, usually the most stable |
| `ddg-html` | `html.duckduckgo.com` (POST) | the classic DuckDuckGo HTML endpoint |
| `mojeek` | `www.mojeek.com` | independent, privacy-minded index; strict rate limits on bursts |
| `bing` | `www.bing.com` | last resort: suspicious clients may receive plausible-but-fake SERPs with no error reported |

When an engine serves a bot-challenge page (HTTP 202/403/429 or a captcha page), the provider automatically falls through to the next engine. If **all** engines return zero results, `web_search` answers "No results found"; if all of them *fail*, the error reports each engine's reason.

> Note: engine behavior varies by IP and network — which engine responds best depends on your connection. The order is configurable (see below). Scraping is tolerated, not guaranteed: an engine may introduce bot-walls at any time.

The plugin is a DSH **bundle**: it is installed into the `web` profile (`~/.dsh/profiles/web`), and its `cordis.patch.yml` layer is composed into the profile at every boot.

Requirements:
- DeepSeek Harness (the `dsh` command) installed.
- [pnpm](https://pnpm.io) on PATH for the official command below (`brew install pnpm`). Option B needs no pnpm.

Run it from anywhere, pointing at the plugin directory:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add /absolute/path/to/dsh-free-search-plugin
```

(or `cd` into the plugin checkout and run `dsh plugin --profile web add .` — a relative path is resolved against the directory you launch the command from, not against the profile).

```sh
mkdir -p ~/.dsh/profiles/web/node_modules
ln -s /absolute/path/to/dsh-free-search-plugin \
      ~/.dsh/profiles/web/node_modules/dsh-web-search-free
```

Bundles are loaded only at boot. Installing does not touch a running server; stop it (Ctrl+C) and start it again:

```sh
dsh web
```

readme.section: What the bundle layer changes in the composition
readme.text:
- inserts a `web-search-free` loader row that mounts the plugin and registers the two providers;
- overrides the seam's `web` row: `searchProvider: free-local`, `fetchProvider: free-local-fetch` (the base layer points at `deepseek-official`).

```sh
node test/smoke.mjs                       # live engine test, needs network
dsh --profile web --dump-config | grep -B2 -A10 "web-search-free"
```

In the dump you should see the `web` row carrying `searchProvider: free-local` (annotated `patched by dsh-web-search-free`) and the inserted `web-search-free` row with its engine list. After the restart, ask the agent something like *"search the web for the latest MLX news"*: the `web_search` tool should return real sources.

In `cordis.patch.yml` (the bundle row) or in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: web-search-free
  config:
    engines: [ddg-lite, ddg-html, mojeek, bing]  # fallback order
    timeoutMs: 15000        # HTTP budget per engine

```yaml
- id: tool-web
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-web'
  config:
    fetch: true          # changed from false

3. select the new preset as the default (or per session).

From then on, the agent can also read the full content of the pages it finds.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-web-search-free
```

pnpm removes the dependency from the profile, and the dsh reconciler drops `dsh-web-search-free` from `dsh.profile.bundles`.

readme.section: Option B — manual (if you installed manually)
readme.text:
1. In `~/.dsh/profiles/web/package.json`, delete the `dsh-web-search-free` key from `dependencies` and its entry from `dsh.profile.bundles`.
2. Remove the link:

```sh
rm ~/.dsh/profiles/web/node_modules/dsh-web-search-free
```

Restart `dsh web` (bundles load at boot). Without this bundle, the seam falls back to the base configuration: `searchProvider: deepseek-official`. The official DeepSeek provider stays registered, so `web_search` works again only if a paid `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` is available (credentials store or environment); otherwise searches fail with a missing-credential error. The plugin's source directory on disk is untouched — delete it separately if you want it gone.

```
lib/index.js          # Cordis plugin (apply/inject/name): registers the providers into ctx.web
lib/engines.js        # search engines + fallback chain
lib/fetch-provider.js # local HTTP(S) fetch provider
lib/html.js           # entity decoding, tag stripping, redirect unwrapping (uddg, bing ck/a)

Zero npm dependencies: only Node >= 20 (global fetch).
No telemetry, no API keys, no accounts. Every search is a plain HTTPS request from your machine to the chosen engine. Engines see your IP and the query, exactly as a browser would.
